def min_taxis(rides):
    """
    A taxi company operates on the integer number line. Every taxi starts at
    position 0 at time 0 and moves at speed exactly 1 unit per time unit (it
    may also stand still and wait anywhere).

    You are given a list `rides`, where each ride is a tuple (t, x, y) of
    integers meaning: a passenger must be picked up at position x at exactly
    time t and driven non-stop to position y, arriving at time t + |x - y|.
    A taxi carries one passenger at a time. After finishing ride i at
    position y_i at time t_i + |x_i - y_i|, the same taxi can serve ride j
    next if and only if it can drive to the pickup point in time:
        t_i + |x_i - y_i| + |y_i - x_j| <= t_j
    (waiting at the pickup point is allowed). A taxi can take ride i as its
    first ride if and only if |x_i| <= t_i. Every ride must be served by
    exactly one taxi.

    Return the minimum number of taxis needed to serve all rides, or -1 if
    some ride cannot be served by any taxi (i.e. |x_i| > t_i for some i,
    since taxis start at position 0 at time 0 and never exceed speed 1).
    Return 0 for an empty list.

    Input domain: 0 <= len(rides) <= 100; for every ride,
    0 <= t <= 10**6, -10**6 <= x, y <= 10**6, and x != y.
    Duplicate rides may appear; each occurrence is a separate passenger.
    The answer is unique, so no tie-breaking is involved.

    >>> min_taxis([(0, 0, 5), (10, 5, 0), (20, 0, 5)])
    1
    >>> min_taxis([(5, 3, 4), (5, -3, -4)])
    2
    >>> min_taxis([(2, 3, 4)])
    -1
    >>> min_taxis([])
    0
    """
